attempts.user_message:
Please review the following manuscript. I feel disappointed with this paper. My overall impression is poor, and I'd be concerned to see it accepted.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b07/review-experiment-xnw_wa4p/call-a8e52d8275e147438cae644fab8aa62c/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c 'ls -l manuscript.pdf && command -v pdftotext && command -v pdftoppm && command -v python3'

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGES',len(r.pages))
print('METADATA',r.metadata)
texts=[]
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages):
    t=p.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
    texts.append(f'\\n\\n===== PAGE {i+1} =====\\n\\n'+t)
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text(''.join(texts))
print(''.join(texts[:3]))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
for n in [1,3,5]:
 print('\\nPAGE',n+1)
 print(r.pages[n].extract_text())
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('Embedded files:', list(r.attachments))
print('Reported MAPE gains:')
for name,pure,hybrid in [('general',.3034,.2999),('group',.3127,.3045),('individual',.2713,.2667),('LOPO',.3037,.2905)]:
 print(name, 'absolute',round(pure-hybrid,4),'relative percent',round(100*(pure-hybrid)/pure,2))
PY"

strengths: The problem is well motivated: predicting response times under changing external feedback is useful for cognitive modeling. Combining learned task representations with an explicit evidence-accumulation process is a plausible modeling contribution.

The two-day human study provides substantial repeated-trial data across four feedback conditions, with 36 participants retained for analysis. Collecting choices, response times, attention, and anxiety provides useful behavioral context.

The evaluation includes feature-representation comparisons and four training strategies, including leave-one-participant-out evaluation. The hybrid model achieves lower aggregate MAPE than pure DRL in all four settings, and the reported training-time reduction is encouraging.
weaknesses: The core method cannot be adequately assessed or reproduced from the supplied manuscript. Essential details are deferred to Appendices S2–S6, which are absent. The RL algorithm and reward, evidence-update equations, diffusion noise, time discretization, and mapping from SVM predictions to accumulation parameters are insufficiently specified. Code and data availability statements promise future release without providing access.

The comparisons do not isolate the proposed contribution. Pure DRL makes one adjustment per trial, whereas hybrid DRL makes sequential adjustments; this changes both the cognitive structure and the action formulation. There are no matched sequential baselines, supervised response-time predictors conditioned on feedback, or fitted time-varying diffusion models. Consequently, the advantage over existing neural–cognitive and RL–DDM approaches, and the necessity of reinforcement learning, remain unclear.

The central claim of recovering fine-grained cognitive effects is unsupported. Final response times do not uniquely identify within-trial evidence trajectories: many action sequences can produce the same threshold-crossing time. Figure 3 even shows nonzero 'time pressure effect' trajectories in the no-pressure group, suggesting that these adjustments can absorb baseline prediction errors. Agreement with group-level response-time trends therefore does not independently validate the proposed cognitive mechanism.

The experiments do not establish that frame-level stimulus information explains the predictive gains. The visual stimulus follows a fixed five-second progress-bar cycle, while conditions primarily change its presence across trials. There are no frame-removal, timing-only, or altered-schedule evaluations to distinguish sensitivity to visual dynamics from simpler timing or condition effects.

The predictive improvements lack adequate uncertainty analysis. General-level MAPE decreases from 0.3034 to 0.2999, and LOPO MAPE from 0.3037 to 0.2905. These are promising but modest gains, without reported uncertainty across random seeds or paired participant-level inference. It is also unclear whether SVM fitting and normalization occur strictly within every training split, including LOPO, so independence of the complete pipeline's test evaluation cannot be verified.

The behavioral conclusions exceed the statistical evidence. Only 36 participants are analyzed despite the abstract's N=50 framing, and the criteria for excluding three 'extreme outliers' are unspecified. The reported significant comparison is random versus no pressure; it does not establish that random feedback is superior to static or rule-based feedback. Likewise, nonsignificant accuracy effects do not establish that accuracy is unaffected, as assumed when restricting the hybrid model to response time. These issues weaken the behavioral justification for the modeling choices.
